## From employer conversations to sponsored learners

Start with relevant commercial teams and a learning-and-development budget owner. Validate the business problem, staff preparation, time availability and funding before counting a company as a buyer. The size and posting signals above guide prospect research; they do not establish demand.

```{=html}
<div class="market-plans">
<article class="market-plan"><span>Focused pilot</span><strong>10 starters</strong><p>25 accounts × 8% × 5 seats</p></article>
<article class="market-plan"><span>Working case</span><strong>40 starters</strong><p>50 accounts × 10% × 8 seats</p></article>
<article class="market-plan"><span>Capacity test</span><strong>150 starters</strong><p>100 accounts × 15% × 10 seats</p></article>
</div>
```

These are illustrative planning cases, not forecasts or commitments. A starter is one learner beginning the certificate, not four course registrations. Program approval, admissions, delivery format and pricing remain pending; the capacity test requires separate staffing validation.

::: {.panel}
### Adjust the national assumptions

```{=html}
<div id="sponsor-model">
<p><label for="sponsor-accounts">Qualified accounts approached (planning range: 0–100)</label><br><input id="sponsor-accounts" type="number" min="0" max="100" step="1" value="50"></p>
<p><label for="sponsor-rate">Assumed sponsor conversion (%)</label><br><input id="sponsor-rate" type="number" min="0" max="100" step="1" value="10"></p>
<p><label for="sponsor-seats">Seats per sponsor</label><br><input id="sponsor-seats" type="number" min="0" max="100" step="1" value="8"></p>
<p><label for="sponsor-fee">Illustrative net certificate tuition ($; 0 means unspecified)</label><br><input id="sponsor-fee" type="number" min="0" max="1000000" step="100" value="0"></p>
<p id="sponsor-result" role="status" aria-live="polite">5 sponsors × 8 seats = 40 certificate starters. Tuition is unspecified.</p>
</div>
<script src="scripts/boston-market.js"></script>
```

Expected starters = accounts × conversion × seats. Tuition receipts = starters × assumed net certificate tuition. Fractional outputs are expected values, not enrollable people. Receipts exclude costs, attrition, payment timing and refunds; they are not profit or NPV. No percentage of the national workforce is assumed to enroll.
:::
